title: Heterogeneous computing in a strongly-connected CPU-GPU environment: fast multiple time-evolution equation-based modeling accelerated using data-driven approach
problem: Solving time-evolution partial differential equations multiple times efficiently while maintaining accuracy and minimizing both computation time and energy consumption is challenging when using only CPU or GPU alone.
motivation: Scientific simulations and engineering applications require efficient PDE solving, making heterogeneous computing approaches critical for achieving both performance and energy efficiency at supercomputing scales.
method: The approach uses CPU-GPU heterogeneous computing on strongly-connected systems (GH200 nodes) with directive-based parallel programming models (OpenMP/OpenACC) for portability. Work is distributed between CPU and GPU to optimize computational load balancing, while data-driven acceleration techniques optimize the equation solving process. Directive-based parallelization orchestrates the heterogeneous computation while maintaining cross-platform portability.
key_novelty: Integration of heterogeneous CPU-GPU computing with data-driven acceleration for time-evolution PDEs using directive-based programming to achieve simultaneous gains in performance, energy, and portability.
contributions: CPU-GPU heterogeneous method achieving 86.4x speedup vs CPU-only and 8.67x vs GPU-only on single nodes with guaranteed accuracy
Energy reduction of 32.2x versus CPU-only (309J from 9944J) and 7.01x versus GPU-only (309J from 2163J)
Supercomputer scalability with 51.6x speedup vs CPU-only and 94.3% weak scaling efficiency up to 1,920 nodes on Alps
Demonstration that directive-based programming models enable effective heterogeneous computing with portability across systems

metrics.speedup: 86.4x vs CPU-only, 8.67x vs GPU-only (single node); 51.6x vs CPU-only, 6.98x vs GPU-only (supercomputer)
metrics.energy: 32.2x reduction vs CPU, 7.01x reduction vs GPU (309J final energy)

limitations: Limitations and trade-offs of the directive-based approach are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous CPU-GPU acceleration for time-evolution PDE solving
